days.title: The Funeral Prayer and Visiting Graves
days.question: How do we pray over the deceased? And why do we visit graves?
days.principle: The funeral prayer over a Muslim is a communal obligation after washing and shrouding him. It is four takbirs while standing, without bowing or prostration. Visiting graves is prescribed to seek mercy for those buried there, ask forgiveness for them, take admonition and remember death.

misconception.peopleSay: When I visit the grave of a righteous person, I ask him himself to help me and fulfil my need.
misconception.correct: Calling on the people of the graves or seeking rescue from them instead of Allah is not prescribed; this is the shirk that all the heavenly messages came to abolish. Visiting graves is prescribed to seek mercy for them and ask forgiveness for them.

days.action: If you can, visit the graves soon and say the Prophet's ﷺ supplication: «السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين...», and let it remind you of death and the Hereafter.
lesson: The funeral prayer is a communal obligation after washing and shrouding the deceased, and it has the same conditions as any prayer: purification, covering the 'awrah and facing the qiblah. It is four takbirs while standing, without bowing or prostration: al-Fatihah after the first, blessings on the Prophet ﷺ after the second, supplication for the deceased after the third and for the Muslims after the fourth, then a single taslim. The Prophet ﷺ said whoever attends the funeral until the prayer has one qirat of reward, and until the burial has two qirats, like two great mountains. Visiting graves is prescribed so that we seek mercy for their people, ask forgiveness for them, take admonition and remember death. But we may not call on the people of the graves or seek rescue from them instead of Allah, because that is shirk. The Prophet ﷺ taught us that if we need something we ask Allah, and if we seek help we seek it from Allah.

quiz.question: Someone went to visit a saint's grave and calls on him to fulfil his need. What is the ruling?
options: Shirk, because calling on the people of the graves and seeking rescue from them instead of Allah is not prescribed
Permissible if the saint was righteous
quiz.explanation: Calling on them or seeking rescue from them instead of Allah is not prescribed, for this is shirk.

quiz.question: What is the legitimate purpose of visiting graves?
options: Remembering death, seeking mercy for those buried and asking forgiveness for them

quiz.question: Does the funeral prayer have bowing and prostration?
options: No, it is four takbirs while standing, without bowing or prostration
quiz.explanation: It is four takbirs while standing, without bowing or prostration.

days.title: Prohibitions Regarding Graves
days.question: Can we build over graves or travel specifically to visit them?
days.principle: It is not permissible to travel specifically to graves, to make them a place of regular gathering, or to build mosques or set lamps over them; nor is it permissible to plaster them, build on them or sit on them.

misconception.peopleSay: Building mosques over the graves of righteous people is a way of honouring them.
misconception.correct: The Prophet ﷺ said in his final illness: «لعن الله اليهود والنصارى اتخذوا قبور أنبيائهم مساجد», and he said of those who built a mosque over the grave of a righteous man: «أولئك شرار الخلق عند الله».

days.action: If you hear that someone plans to travel specifically to visit a grave, politely share with him the hadith «لا تشد الرحال إلا إلى ثلاث مساجد».
lesson: The book specifies things that are forbidden regarding graves. The first is setting out on a journey, meaning travelling specifically to graves, because the Prophet ﷺ said journeys are not to be undertaken except to three mosques: al-Masjid al-Haram, his mosque and al-Masjid al-Aqsa. Also, graves may not be made a place of regular gathering, and the Prophet ﷺ said: do not make my grave a place of gathering, and send blessings on me, for your blessings reach me. In his final illness the Prophet ﷺ cursed the Jews and Christians who took the graves of their prophets as places of worship. He forbade plastering a grave, building over it and sitting on it, and said that sitting on a burning coal that burns one's clothes is better than sitting on a grave. The sunnah is that a grave is not raised much, about a hand-span, as the scholars mentioned.
days.quote: Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I dislike that a created being be venerated to the point that his grave is made a place of worship, fearing trial for him and for the people after him.

quiz.question: People travel specifically to visit a certain grave to seek blessing from it. What is the ruling on this travel?
options: Permissible if the grave is a prophet's
Forbidden; setting out on a journey is only for the three mosques

quiz.question: What is the ruling on building a mosque over a grave?
options: Forbidden, and the Prophet ﷺ cursed those who took the graves of their prophets as places of worship

quiz.question: What is the ruling on sitting on graves?

days.title: Patience in Calamity, and Wailing
days.question: Is crying over the dead haram? And what is the difference between grief and wailing?
days.principle: Wailing over the dead, slapping the cheeks and showing panic and resentment are practices of the Jahiliyyah that Allah and His Messenger detest. Mourning (ihdad) for a deceased person may not exceed three days, except for a husband, for whom it is four months and ten days.

misconception.peopleSay: Any crying or tear over the dead is haram and causes the dead to be punished.
misconception.correct: Allah does not punish for the grief of the heart or the tears of the eye, for that is mercy; He punishes only for wailing and showing panic and resentment. The Prophet ﷺ wept and said: «هذه رحمة جعلها الله في قلوب عباده».

days.action: If someone you know has lost a loved one, console them with the Prophet's ﷺ words «إن لله ما أخذ وله ما أعطى وكل شيء عنده بأجل مسمى», and remind them of patience and hoping for reward.
lesson: The book distinguishes between natural grief and wailing. Wailing, slapping the cheeks, tearing clothes and showing panic are practices of the Jahiliyyah, and the Prophet ﷺ said: whoever does that is not one of us. The Prophet ﷺ disowned the woman who raises her voice, the one who shaves her head and the one who tears her clothes. He warned that the deceased may be punished for wailing over him if it was his way, or he requested it, or he neglected to forbid his family from it. But tears of the eye and grief of the heart are mercy; the Prophet ﷺ himself wept when he saw his grandson dying, and said that Allah does not punish for the tears of the eye or the grief of the heart. Mourning for any deceased person is three days only, except a wife for her husband, four months and ten days.
days.quote: Allah, Majestic and Exalted, does not punish for the grief of the heart or the tears of the eye, for that is part of the mercy He places in the hearts of whomever He wills of His merciful servants.

quiz.question: Someone lost a loved one; his eyes shed tears and his heart is grieving. Does this contradict patience?
options: It is a deficiency in faith
No, tears of the eye and grief of the heart are mercy and are not punished
quiz.explanation: Allah, Majestic and Exalted, does not punish for the grief of the heart or the tears of the eye, for that is part of the mercy He places in the hearts of whomever He wills of His merciful servants.

quiz.question: A woman's brother died. How long may she mourn for him?
options: Three days only; only for a husband is mourning four months and ten days

quiz.question: What is the ruling on shaving the head or slapping the cheeks at a calamity?
options: Among the practices of the Jahiliyyah that Allah and His Messenger detest
quiz.explanation: The one who shaves (al-haliqah) is the woman who shaves her head at a calamity.

days.title: Zakah: Purification and Solidarity
days.question: Why did Allah make zakah obligatory? And on what is it due?
days.principle: Giving zakah is a pillar of Islam. The conditions for it being due are Islam, freedom, owning the threshold amount (nisab) and the passing of a year where that is required. Allah legislated it to purify the soul of stinginess and selfishness, to support the poor and deprived, and to establish the public good.

misconception.peopleSay: Zakah is optional: whoever wants to pay it pays it, and whoever doesn't is free not to.
misconception.correct: Giving zakah is a pillar of Islam: whoever withholds it out of denial has disbelieved, and whoever withholds it out of stinginess has it taken from him by force and is disciplined for that.

days.action: If you have wealth, find out today whether it has reached the nisab and a year has passed over it, and set a date to review your zakah.
lesson: Zakah is a pillar of Islam, and it becomes due with conditions: Islam, freedom, owning the nisab, and a year passing for the kinds of wealth where that is required. Allah legislated it to purify the soul of stinginess and selfishness, support the poor and establish the public good. Whoever withholds it out of denial has disbelieved, and whoever withholds it out of stinginess has it taken from him by force and is disciplined. The Quran and Sunnah contain a severe warning for those who hoard gold and silver without paying what is due on them. Abu Bakr mobilised armies to fight those who withheld zakah and said that if they withheld even a rope they used to give to the Prophet ﷺ, he would fight them over it. Zakah is due on gold, silver, modern currencies and trade goods, and the nisab of gold is twenty mithqals, equal to 92 grams.
days.quote: A severe warning against withholding zakah has come in the Noble Quran and the authentic Sunnah.

quiz.question: Someone has money that reached the nisab and withholds zakah out of stinginess, not denial. What is the ruling?
options: It is taken from him by force and he is disciplined
quiz.explanation: And whoever withholds it out of stinginess has it taken from him by force and is disciplined for that.

quiz.question: What is the consequence in the Hereafter for someone who withholds the zakah of his wealth?
options: His wealth decreases in this world only
His wealth will be made into a serpent that coils around him on the Day of Resurrection

quiz.question: Why did Allah legislate zakah?
options: To reduce the money of the rich
To purify the soul of stinginess and support the poor
quiz.explanation: Allah the Exalted legislated it as a purification of the soul from stinginess and selfishness, and as support for the poor and deprived.

askTheBook: What are the conditions for zakah being due?

days.title: The Zakah of Livestock and Crops
days.question: Does a farmer or livestock owner owe zakah? And how much?
days.principle: Zakah is due on livestock: camels, cattle and sheep. It is due on grains and fruits, whose nisab is five wasqs, and the amount due differs with the means of irrigation: on what is irrigated with effort and cost, half a tenth, and on what is watered by the sky, a tenth.

misconception.peopleSay: The nisab of gold is established by many authentic hadiths.
misconception.correct: Al-Nawawi said: No statement of the nisab of gold has come in the authentic hadiths; hadiths fixing its nisab at twenty mithqals have come, but they are weak; however, those whose consensus counts agreed on it.

days.action: If you have land or livestock, or know someone who does, review with them the zakah threshold as the book mentions it, and if there are more details, ask the people of knowledge.
lesson: Zakah is not only on money; it is also on livestock and crops. For camels, the first nisab is five and a sheep is due; for cattle it is thirty and a one-year-old calf is due; and for sheep it is forty and one sheep is due. Beyond that, the Sunnah explained the thresholds and amounts in detail, and Abu Bakr's letter to Anas contains them. For grains and fruits the nisab is five wasqs, and a wasq is sixty sa' by agreement. The amount differs according to irrigation: what is watered by rain or springs is a tenth, and what is irrigated with effort and cost is half a tenth. The book quotes al-Nawawi that the nisab of gold has no authentic hadith, but there is consensus on it.
days.quote: Mujahid explained ﴿طَيِّبَاتِ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ﴾ (al-Baqarah 267) as lawful trade.

quiz.question: A farmer's land is watered by rain, and his neighbour irrigates his with a pump at a cost. Is the zakah the same?
options: No, rain-watered is a tenth, and what is irrigated at cost is half a tenth
The one with the pump pays more
There is no zakah on crops
quiz.explanation: On what is irrigated with effort and cost, half a tenth; and on what is watered by the sky, a tenth.

quiz.question: Someone has 40 freely grazing sheep. Is zakah due on them?
options: No, they don't reach the nisab
quiz.explanation: The nisab for sheep is forty, and one sheep is due on them.

quiz.question: From what does a merchant pay zakah?
options: From his lawful earnings from trade
quiz.explanation: Mujahid explained ﴿طَيِّبَاتِ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ﴾ (al-Baqarah 267) as lawful trade.

days.title: The Recipients of Zakah, and Zakat al-Fitr
days.question: To whom does zakah go? And what is zakat al-fitr?
days.principle: Allah Himself set out the recipients of zakah in the Quran: the poor, the needy, those who work on it, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, freeing captives, debtors, in the cause of Allah, and the stranded traveller. Zakat al-fitr is obligatory; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made it obligatory as a purification for the fasting person from idle and indecent talk and as food for the poor and needy.

misconception.peopleSay: Any charity to relatives has less reward than charity to a stranger.
misconception.correct: The Sunnah made a Muslim's charity to a relative both charity and maintaining kinship. The Prophet ﷺ said of Zaynab, the wife of Ibn Mas'ud: «لها أجران، أجر القرابة وأجر الصدقة».

days.action: If you have a relative in need, consider starting your charity with them (excluding parents, grandparents, children and grandchildren for zakah), because charity to relatives is both charity and maintaining kinship.
lesson: Allah Himself set out in the Quran the eight recipients of zakah: the poor, the needy, those who work on it, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, freeing captives, debtors, in the cause of Allah, and the stranded traveller. There is a well-known disagreement about whether "in the cause of Allah" includes public interests. Charity to relatives is charity and maintaining kinship, but a person may not give his zakah to his ascendants or descendants, because he is obliged to support them. The wife of Ibn Mas'ud asked the Prophet ﷺ about spending on her husband and the orphans in her care, and he said she would have two rewards: the reward of kinship and the reward of charity. Charity is not lawful for the family of Muhammad ﷺ, to the point that he took a date out of the mouth of al-Hasan or al-Husayn. The book also begins talking about zakat al-fitr, which the Prophet ﷺ made obligatory as a purification for the fasting person and food for the needy.
days.quote: A man may not give zakah to his ascendants, however far up, nor to his descendants, however far down, because he is obliged to support them.

quiz.question: Someone wants to give his zakah to his poor father. Is that allowed?
options: Yes, he has more right than a stranger
Yes, if he is very poor
No, because supporting one's ascendants and descendants is already obligatory on him
quiz.explanation: A man may not give zakah to his ascendants, however far up, nor to his descendants, however far down, because he is obliged to support them.

quiz.question: You gave charity to a poor relative (not a parent, grandparent, child or grandchild). What is your reward?
options: Two rewards: the reward of kinship and the reward of charity

quiz.question: May the family of the Prophet ﷺ take from charity?
options: No, the family of Muhammad ﷺ does not consume charity

days.title: Fasting Ramadan: Its Reality and Rulings
days.question: When does Ramadan begin? And what is the reality of fasting: is it just abstaining from food?
days.principle: Fasting Ramadan is a pillar of Islam. It becomes obligatory by sighting the crescent when the sky is clear, or by completing thirty days of Sha'ban when it is cloudy. The reality of fasting is abstaining from all physical and moral things that break the fast from dawn until sunset.

misconception.peopleSay: Fasting is just not eating or drinking; nothing else I do matters.
misconception.correct: The reality of fasting is abstaining from all physical and moral things that break it. «من لم يدع قول الزور والعمل به فليس لله حاجة في أن يدع طعامه وشرابه».

days.action: On your next fasting day (or today if you are not fasting), choose to avoid lying and false speech completely, and remember the hadith «من لم يدع قول الزور والعمل به».
lesson: Fasting Ramadan is a pillar of Islam, and it begins with sighting the crescent; if the sky is cloudy, we complete thirty days of Sha'ban. The book says what is relied on is sighting by eye, and that if the crescent is sighted in one country, it binds the countries that share part of the night with it, according to the more correct of the scholars' two views. The reality of fasting is not only staying away from food and drink; it is staying away from all physical and moral things that break the fast from dawn to sunset. The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever does not give up false speech, Allah has no need for him to give up his food and drink. It is sunnah to hasten breaking the fast and to delay the pre-dawn meal, and the Prophet ﷺ said there is blessing in the pre-dawn meal. 'Adi ibn Hatim misunderstood the white and black threads and put two ropes under his pillow, so the Prophet ﷺ explained to him that they are the darkness of night and the brightness of day.
days.quote: And that the people of knowledge should strive to unite the Ummah on this question upon a common word.

quiz.question: Someone is fasting but lies and curses all day. Has his fast achieved its meaning?
options: Yes, as long as he didn't eat
Yes, words have nothing to do with it
No, the reality of fasting is abstaining from physical and moral things that break it
quiz.explanation: The reality of fasting is abstaining from all physical and moral things that break the fast, from dawn until sunset.

quiz.question: It is the last day of Sha'ban, the sky is cloudy and no one saw the crescent. What do we do?
What is meant by the white and black threads in the verse of fasting?
options: The brightness of day and the darkness of night
The colour of the sky at sunset

days.title: Rulings on Breaking the Fast, and Recommended and Forbidden Fasts
days.question: What happens if I eat by mistake while fasting? And which days are recommended or forbidden to fast?
days.principle: Whoever deliberately breaks the fast by intercourse must make it up and pay the expiation, and whoever forgets and eats or drinks should complete his fast. Among the recommended fasts are six days of Shawwal, the day of 'Arafah, 'Ashura' and the White Days; among the forbidden fasts are fasting every day of one's life and fasting the two days of 'Eid.

misconception.peopleSay: Whoever eats or drinks by mistake in Ramadan has ruined his fast and must break it.
misconception.correct: «من نسي وهو صائم فأكل أو شرب فليتم صومه فإنما أطعمه الله وسقاه».

days.action: Choose one of the voluntary fasts in the book (such as Mondays and Thursdays or the White Days) and plan to fast it this week or this month.
lesson: The book continues the rulings of fasting: the Prophet ﷺ said eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum calls the adhan, because he calls it at dawn, and said that people will remain in good as long as they hasten to break the fast. A man came saying he was ruined because he had intercourse with his wife in Ramadan; the Prophet ﷺ asked him about the expiation in order, and in the end gave him dates to feed his family. Whoever eats or drinks by mistake completes his fast, because Allah is the One who fed him and gave him drink. Among the recommended fasts are six days of Shawwal, the day of 'Arafah which expiates two years, 'Ashura' which expiates one year, the White Days, and Mondays and Thursdays. The fast most beloved to Allah is the fast of Dawud: fasting one day and not the next. But fasting every day of one's life is forbidden, and the Prophet ﷺ said: whoever fasts forever has not fasted.

quiz.question: Someone fasting forgot and drank water. What about his fast?
options: Valid, and he completes his fast
Invalid, and he makes it up
He makes it up and pays expiation
He breaks his fast for the rest of the day

quiz.question: Which voluntary fast is most beloved to Allah?
options: Fasting every day of one's life
Fasting every day without a break
The fast of Dawud: fasting one day and not the next

quiz.question: What is the virtue of fasting the day of 'Arafah for someone not on Hajj?
options: It expiates the past year and the coming year

days.title: Night Prayer, I'tikaf and Laylat al-Qadr
days.question: How do I make the most of the nights of Ramadan? And when do I seek Laylat al-Qadr?
days.principle: Among the emphasised sunnahs of Ramadan is reviving its nights with prayer, and the number of units of the night prayer is a matter with latitude. I'tikaf and reviving the whole night in the last ten nights are recommended, as is seeking Laylat al-Qadr on their odd nights.

misconception.peopleSay: The Ramadan night prayer has only one number of units, and anyone who prays more or fewer is wrong.
misconception.correct: His ﷺ night prayer in Ramadan and at other times was eleven units, and the number of units of the night prayer is a matter with latitude.

days.action: For the coming last ten nights of Ramadan, make a plan to revive the odd nights, and wake your family with you as the Prophet ﷺ used to do.
lesson: The book begins with the days on which fasting is forbidden: the day of al-Fitr and the day of al-Adha, and the days of tashriq except for someone who cannot find a sacrificial animal; a menstruating woman does not fast, and she makes up the fast but not the prayer. Among the emphasised sunnahs of Ramadan is reviving its nights with prayer; the Prophet ﷺ prayed eleven units in Ramadan and at other times, and there is latitude in the number. Aisha described his prayer: four units, do not ask about their beauty and length, then four like them, then three. When the last ten began, he would tighten his waist-wrap, revive his night and wake his family, and he would perform i'tikaf in them. Whoever prays the nights of Ramadan or Laylat al-Qadr out of faith and hoping for reward, his previous sins are forgiven. The Prophet ﷺ commanded us to seek Laylat al-Qadr on the odd nights of the last ten.

quiz.question: Your friend says: "Taraweeh must be exactly 8 units or the prayer is invalid." What is the correct understanding?
options: The number of units of the night prayer is a matter with latitude

quiz.question: A woman missed fasting and prayers because of menstruation. What does she make up?
options: The fasts only, not the prayers

quiz.question: Where do we seek Laylat al-Qadr?
options: On the first night of Ramadan
In the middle of the month
On the odd nights of the last ten

days.title: Hajj: The Obligation of a Lifetime
days.question: Is Hajj obligatory on everyone? And how many times in a lifetime?
days.principle: Hajj is a pillar of Islam and an obligation from Allah on those able. It is obligatory once in a lifetime and anything more is voluntary. The conditions of its obligation are Islam, puberty, sanity and ability, and its pillars are ihram, tawaf, sa'y and standing at 'Arafah.

misconception.peopleSay: Sa'y between Safa and Marwah isn't important; the verse said "there is no blame", meaning there's no problem if you don't do it.
misconception.correct: Aisha said: «ما أتم الله حج امرئ ولا عمرته لم يطف بين الصفا والمروة», and if it were as you say, it would have said "there is no blame on him if he does not go between them". The verse was revealed about the Ansar, who disliked going between them because of what they used to do in the Jahiliyyah.

days.action: If you have not yet performed Hajj, make a sincere intention to perform it when Allah grants you the ability, and start learning its four pillars today.
lesson: Hajj is a pillar of Islam and an obligation on those able, and the Muslims agree that it is obligatory on whoever is able. It is obligatory once in a lifetime and anything more is voluntary; when a man asked the Prophet ﷺ, "Every year?", he said that had he said yes, it would have become obligatory and you would not have been able. The conditions of its obligation are Islam, puberty, sanity and ability, and its pillars are ihram, tawaf, sa'y and standing at 'Arafah; the Prophet ﷺ said Hajj is 'Arafah. The rites are three: ifrad, qiran and tamattu'; those performing qiran and tamattu' must offer a sacrifice, and whoever cannot find one fasts three days during Hajj and seven when he returns. Whoever performs Hajj without obscenity or sin returns like the day his mother bore him, and the reward of an accepted Hajj is Paradise. Aisha corrected 'Urwah's understanding of the verse: the words "there is no blame" were revealed because the Ansar felt uneasy about sa'y, not because sa'y is unimportant.
days.quote: That Hajj is obligatory on whoever is able is something the Muslims agree on by a necessary consensus, and it is known of the religion of Islam by necessity.

quiz.question: Someone performed Hajj once and wants to do it again. What is the ruling on the second Hajj?
options: Voluntary, because Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime
quiz.explanation: And that it is obligatory once in a lifetime, and anything more is voluntary.

quiz.question: Someone wants to perform Hajj but cannot afford it. Is Hajj obligatory on him?
options: No, ability is a condition of the obligation
quiz.explanation: That Hajj is obligatory on whoever is able is something the Muslims agree on by a necessary consensus, and it is known of the religion of Islam by necessity.

quiz.question: Someone performed Hajj but did not do sa'y between Safa and Marwah. Is his Hajj complete?
